summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would change export and trade laws, mainly by updating the Export Market Development Grants scheme and renaming the Australian Trade Commission.

The government would cut some eligible spending categories, cap the free sample category at $15,000, raise the daily overseas allowance from $300 to $350, and let Austrade use money from other sources for scheme administration.
The bill would also give the Australian Trade Commission a new name that includes 'Investment' and require the next scheme review to be finished by a date the Minister sets.
changes: Removes communications as an eligible expenditure category.
Limits free sample expenditure to $15,000, with an exception for claimants combining two years of spending that includes 2015-16.
Describes promotional literature or other advertising to cover electronic or other forms.
Repeals reimbursement for in-country travel except air fares and raises the daily allowance for overseas visits from $300 to $350.
Allows Austrade to direct funds from other sources to cover EMDG administration costs.
Removes the requirement for an independent review to start on a set date and instead lets the Minister set the completion date for the next review.
summary.affected: Exporters who use the Export Market Development Grants scheme and the Australian Trade Commission (to be renamed the Australian Trade and Investment Commission) would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Trade Legislation Amendment Bill (No.1) 2016, which renames Austrade to the Australian Trade and Investment Commission and makes technical changes to the Export Market Development Grants scheme, including removing sunset clauses and updating expenditure categories. The speaker also criticised the government's foreign investment policies, citing Business Council of Australia concerns that new FIRB thresholds and fees deter investment.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Trade Legislation Amendment Bill (No. 1) 2016, which makes minor amendments to the Export Market Development Grants scheme to improve its operation, including removing sunset provisions, capping free sample expenditure at $15,000, and requiring an independent review by 2021. The speaker cited success stories such as Xelon Entertainment ($1.5 million in export sales) and SAGE Automation ($40 million revenue), and noted KPMG modelling that each dollar of grants generates $7 in benefits.

speeches.speaker: Wyatt Roy
speeches.brief: The Trade Legislation Amendment Bill (No. 1) 2016 should be passed to make the Export Market Development Grants scheme evergreen, removing its four-yearly sunset provisions to reduce uncertainty for exporters. In 2013-14, over 3,100 recipients received $141 million in grants, averaging $44,270 each, with the scheme enjoying bipartisan support since 1974.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Export Market Development Grants scheme should be made permanent without sunset clauses, noting that the government increased funding to $137.9 million and highlighting the scheme's $7 return per dollar invested. He criticised Labor for previously cutting the scheme from $200 million to $125 million and for proposing a 50% capital gains tax increase.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: The Trade Legislation Amendment Bill (No. 1) 2016 extends the Export Market Development Grants scheme beyond 30 June 2016, with over 3,100 recipients receiving $141 million in grants averaging $44,270 each. The bill implements minor policy and technical amendments, including removing communications as an eligible expense, capping free sample expenditure at $15,000, and renaming the Australian Trade Commission to the Australian Trade and Investment Commission.
